newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity higher ahead of April expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity higher ahead of April expiry.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were higher Tuesday in what was primarily a technical move ahead of the expiry of the April contracts today, industry sources said.
Most of the upmove could be attributed to shortcovering, the sources said.
"What we are seeing is the squeezing out of the shorts again, the same situation we saw yesterday," said a New York-based futures trader.

As of 1210 EST, April California Oregon Border (COB) was up 23 cents at $11.10 per megawatt hour (MWh) after exchanges as low as $10.60, while May COB was up 15 cents at $10.10 after trade as low as $9.95 per MWh.
COB deferreds were also higher, with August up 15 cents at $17.75 and September up 10 cents at $17.90 per MWh.
April Palo Verde (PV) was 24 cents higher at $14.90 after reaching as low as $14.50, while May PV was up 20 cents at $14.50 after reaching as low as $14.35 per MWh.
July PV was up 12 cents at $20.20 per MWh.
Both the COB and PV April contracts expire today.
NYMEX said that as of 1140 EST, an estimated total of 52 COB and 81 PV contracts had traded.

Restart of the 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant in California is expected on April 1. The unit, which has been down for refueling, maintenance and unplanned repairs since November 30, needs additional maintenance work to replace gaskets associated with access points into the steam generator.
The plant's 1,080 MW unit 3 is still scheduled to begin a refueling outage April 12.
Also, Arizona Public Service Co's 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear unit 1 was reduced to 62 percent of capacity as of Tuesday morning to repair a low pressure feedwater heater tube leak.

Separately, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear unit in Washington state was tentatively scheduled to shut down by mid-week. The unit will begin an annual refueling outage April 18, but has been expected to shut down ahead of that date due to a regional oversupply of lower-cost hydropower.

In the Northwest, temperatures were forecast to average about 15 degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the northeast section for the rest of the week, while readings along the coast would run normal to two degrees Fahrenheit above normal.
In the Southwest, temperatures would run above normal across the region with the northeastern area averaging 12 degrees above seasonal norms.
As of 1225 EST, NYMEX May Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up 6.4 cents at $1.905 per million British thermal units.
COB open interest for March 25 fell 197 to 3,694 while PV open interest fell 158 to 3,326, NYMEX said.
